chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! I supplicate Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that He grant me the halal (permissible sustenance).' He said: 'Do you know what is the halal?' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! As for that which is with us, it is the goodly earnings.' He said: 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: The halal is the food of the Chosen Ones, but say: I ask You from Your extensive sustenance.'

key_terms.قُوتُ الْمُصْطَفَيْنَ: Food/Sustenance of the Chosen Ones (Prophets and Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between asking for halal sustenance and the specific du'a of the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between the general legal definition of halal (permissible earnings) and the spiritual elevation sought by the Ahl al-Bayt, who emphasize 'extensive sustenance' (rizq al-wasi') as a sign of divine favor. By referencing the practice of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), the text underscores a Shia scholarly tradition that prioritizes abundance and quality of provision over mere legality, reflecting the high station of the Chosen Ones.
